A1.justification: Both PDFs are 35-page versions of the same Hinge Regression Tree paper. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–K without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic convergence and approximation experiments, HRT regression benchmark results, step-size ablations in Appendix G and binary-classification results in Appendix K. These include original outcomes despite some baseline scores being attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains original synthetic experiments, regression results, Appendix G ablations and five-dataset classification results in Table 14. Removing MSLR does not eliminate the paper's original empirical contributions.

M1.justification: The hinge-based splitting objective, damped Newton/OLS updates, ridge option, fallback strategy, initialization and Algorithms 1–4 are unchanged. The binary-classification adaptation in Appendix K was already present in v1.

E1.justification: v2 removes MSLR, reducing the regression benchmark suite from 14 to 13 datasets. This removes query–URL relevance prediction with 136 features and 964,933 samples (Appendix J, Table 13). Synthetic tasks and all five classification datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every retained comparison, including DTSemNet, DGT, TAO-A/O, CART, XGBoost, M5 and linear trees where previously evaluated. The entire MSLR benchmark comparison is deleted; no retained experiment changes its comparator set.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same data splits, five-fold cross-validation, metrics, sample sizes and reported training settings. MSLR is removed without a replacement experiment or a revised protocol for the remaining benchmarks.

E4.justification: The convergence illustrations, synthetic residual visualizations and Appendix G step-size/fallback analyses are unchanged. Tables 5–8 retain the same studies on sinc, twisted sigmoid, Kinematics and D-Ailerons.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts, standard-deviation reporting and p < 0.05 significance markers are unchanged. Table 1 retains ten repetitions for 2D functions and five for 3D functions; regression and classification performance tables retain their five-run reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 2 deletes the MSLR result row, including HRT RMSE 0.764 ± 0.000, XGBoost 0.750 ± 0.000 and DTSemNet 0.766 ± 0.000, together with the other comparator entries. All retained scores, rankings and qualitative findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Newton/OLS derivation, convergence assumptions and proof, complexity analysis, universal approximation theorem and dimensionality corollary are unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–F.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same method, Newton-equivalence, convergence, approximation and accuracy/compactness claims. The benchmark deletion does not produce a substantive revision of these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 removes MSLR from its examples but retains the same scalability interpretation, now citing YearPred alone. Explanations of damping, fallback behavior and compactness, along with conditioning and dimensionality limitations, are unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 11 removes the MSLR configuration block, including HRT's depth 3, ridge strength 0, step size 0.5 and threshold 0.2. Appendix J and Table 13 remove its dataset description and source link. Other implementation details, hyperparameters and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the research bibliography are unchanged. The relationships to hinging hyperplanes, TAO, DGT and DTSemNet, including novelty positioning, are retained; the removed MSLR URL concerns dataset access.

P1.justification: Language edits are limited to deleting MSLR mentions from Section 5.3 and its short Appendix J description, plus updating the arXiv version/date stamp. The narrative, terminology and section sequence remain stable.

P2.justification: Tables 2, 11 and 13 lose their MSLR rows or block. Table 13 moves from page 34 to page 33, while Appendix K's opening moves to page 34, grouping the dataset and classification material more coherently. Figures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Removing MSLR deletes the largest benchmark and the query–URL relevance-prediction evidence, modestly weakening support for Section 5.3's retained scalability interpretation. Clearer grouping of Appendices J–K is a small presentation benefit, but no replacement evidence is provided. The unchanged method, theory and remaining experiments limit the overall decline.
